label: LLM & GenAI
description: Prompting, agents, evaluation, safety, latency, and cost.

questions.prompt: You are building an LLM feature for customers. How do you decide whether prompting is enough or fine-tuning is justified?
questions.followUp: What evidence would make you approve a fine-tuning project?
questions.idealAnswer: Establish a prompt and retrieval baseline on a representative evaluation set. Fine-tune when a stable repeated behavior or style gap remains, data quality is high, and measured gains justify training and maintenance cost—not to inject changing facts.

questions.prompt: Design an evaluation system for an AI assistant whose answers are partly subjective.
questions.followUp: How would you keep an LLM judge honest?
questions.idealAnswer: Define task-specific rubrics, curate difficult representative cases, combine deterministic checks with calibrated human and model judgments, prefer blinded pairwise comparisons, and monitor disagreement. Regularly calibrate judges against expert labels.

questions.prompt: When should an LLM use tools, and how do you stop an agent loop from becoming unsafe?
questions.followUp: Which tool actions need a confirmation step?
questions.idealAnswer: Use tools for fresh data and deterministic actions. Provide narrow schemas and least-privilege credentials, validate arguments and outputs, cap iterations and spend, isolate untrusted content, and require confirmation for irreversible or externally visible actions.

questions.prompt: An LLM workflow is accurate but too slow and expensive. What is your optimization order?
questions.followUp: Where can a smaller model safely replace a large one?
questions.idealAnswer: Trace latency and token cost by stage, remove redundant context, cache stable results, parallelize independent calls, route simple tasks to smaller models, and reserve larger models for uncertain cases. Re-evaluate quality after every change.

questions.prompt: Explain prompt injection as a system-design problem, not just a bad-prompt problem.
questions.followUp: How would you treat instructions found inside retrieved documents?
questions.idealAnswer: Model instructions and external content cross different trust boundaries. Treat retrieved or browsed content as untrusted data, keep authorization outside the model, minimize tool permissions, validate outputs, and never let text grant capabilities.
